page: Microsoft Azure E64ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

The instance is configured with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 3780 GB NVMe SSD and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. This combination of high-capacity memory and fast local solid-state storage supports workloads requiring low-latency data access without the need for dedicated GPU hardware, as the GPU count is zero.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The system achieves top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core tests, and software compilation. Memory bandwidth is robust, with read-only cached speeds reaching 4509.39 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 246.15 GB/sec. Database operations, Redis SET operations at 84.54 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput also rank in the top tier. Additionally, the hardware-assisted AMX instructions contribute to strong prompt processing speeds during LLM inference.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E64ds_v6 offers high resource density, balancing a large memory footprint with substantial local NVMe storage on a dedicated CPU allocation. This makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive and database-heavy workloads. Recommended applications include large relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data analytics, software compilation pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
